title: Armour the bullet holes?
hook: Returning bombers are riddled on the wings. So armour the wings. Or is that backwards?

doesNotKnow: how the way data is collected can hide the cases that matter

misconception: The places where returning planes show the most damage are the places that most need armour.
objective: The learner can explain that only survivors are inspected, so the spots with few holes on survivors are where a hit was fatal, and that missing cases can be the signal.

claims.text: In the lesson's model, bullets land evenly over the plane and only an engine hit brings a plane down, so planes that come back never have engine holes.
claims.source: Toy model, by construction: src/demos/probability/armour-where-no-holes/model.ts (3 hits per plane, uniform over the silhouette; lost = any hit inside an engine ellipse). The lesson says it is a toy model.

claims.text: With the stage's silhouette about 15% of the plane's area is engine, so a plane taking 3 hits is lost about 38% of the time; of the first 100 seeded planes, 35 were lost and the 65 that came back had 0 engine holes.
claims.source: model.ts engineShare() = 0.147 on a 0.25-unit grid; 1 - (1 - 0.147)^3 = 0.379. fleet(1943): first 10 planes 5 lost; first 60, 23 lost; first 100, 35 lost; first 400, 141 lost; engine holes on returned planes 0 in every case.

claims.text: During the Second World War the statistician Abraham Wald analysed damage on returning aircraft and reasoned that the areas with few hits on survivors were the vulnerable ones.
claims.source: M. Mangel and F. J. Samaniego (1984), 'Abraham Wald's work on aircraft survivability', Journal of the American Statistical Association 79(386): 259-267. (The brief spelled the second author 'Samaniuk'; the author is Francisco J. Samaniego.)

recall.question: A study of successful start-ups finds most founders dropped out of college. Why is that weak evidence that dropping out helps?
options: It only looks at the start-ups that survived
recall.why: Dropouts whose companies failed are not in the data. Like planes that never came back, the missing cases could tell the opposite story.
